overall_summary: Space-themed mysteries and mind-bending animal paradoxes are driving the highest views and engagement on the channel. Conversely, repetitive psychology topics and brain-related facts are currently underperforming and failing to capture audience interest.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Largest Ocean in Space Will Mind-Blow You!' (460 views) and 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' (368 views) are the top-performing videos.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on space topics that connect cosmic scale to everyday human senses (smell, taste, touch).

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' (302 views) and 'This Animal Literally Dies Every Winter!' (179 views) show strong relative performance.
winning_patterns.action: Create content comparing familiar natural elements in shocking, historically or biologically counter-intuitive ways.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views on first upload, 54 on second) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently underperform.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from generic brain/memory facts unless they can be framed with a highly unusual, high-stakes hook.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'AI Recreates Pink Floyd Song From Brain Waves!' generated only 34 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid overly technical or niche pop-culture science stories that lack broad, immediate curiosity appeal.

next_video.concept: A planet where it literally rains molten iron.
next_video.opening_direction: Start with: 'Imagine a world where the evening breeze is made of vaporized metal...'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that on planet WASP-76b, temperatures are so extreme that iron evaporates, condenses, and falls as liquid metal rain at night.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful space category combined with a vivid sensory hook (molten iron rain), keeping the duration at a tight, high-retention 15 seconds.

experiment: Test a 'Time & History Paradox' concept comparing ancient human history timelines to cosmic timelines to see if history-focused paradoxes can replicate the success of the shark/tree video.
